notes.body:
## Recap vorige sessie
- We sealed away the Death Tyrant on the island of the Chimera
- We found a large deal of treasure on the beach (on the beach!)
- We arrived on the [island of the fates](wiki:island-of-the-fates)
- We found [Mezz](wiki:mezz) who offered us the services of a Doppelganger to impersonate [Gaius](wiki:gaius).

## This session
Starting at [OOTD Day](wiki:) 1, morning (7:00? 8:00?)

We go to [The fates](wiki:the-fates).

Our funds:
- [Yendithas](wiki:yendithas): 214g
- [Brax](wiki:brax): 4444g
- [Thyphoon](wiki:thyphoon): 1300g
- [Atyche](wiki:atyche): 527g

444.4 + 21.4 + 130 + 52.7p
- 648,5

The guardian of the Fates immediately guides us in. We follow the same route as last time.
The deeper we walk inside, the stronger is the feeling that we're being watched. It gets slimier and slimier. It seems like we see eyes from the corners of our... Well, eyes.

Apparently the loom of the fates is made from the chestcage of a dragon.
There is a blind Medusa cleaning in the corner.

We see our own tapestries - with a moebius strip looping around back to here.

Decema is still flirty, Granny Morta is acting like a witch.

Aaaand we manage to do nothing, since they wanted platinum pieces, not gold pieces or anything else. Damnit.

Brax asks what a level up would cost: 
- your breath
- your body resilience
- or your victories.
From Brax alone.
He does not.

We set sail for [Island of Yonder](wiki:island-of-yonder).
We sacrifice a White Ox.

We sail for about 8 hours. Then, we see a ship sailing on the horizon - with red sails.
- I *very* vaguely remember that the color "red" means something. But what... (*rolled a 7 for history*).
- On the sail is a logo of a spiral with 8 dots on it, surrounding a red star.
- Everyone except for me suddenly remembers it - when we went to the Mythral mines. [Hamun Kost](wiki:hamun-kost)! The guy we will kill on day 9 or day 10, on the way to [Mytros](wiki:mytros) from the Mithral Mines.
- We pass by the ship at around a range of 300 feet. He sails himself, and the deck is filled with a crew of skeletons.
This was around 17:00 (day 1).

![](media/sign-of-hamun-kost.jpg)

![](media/hamun-kost.jpg)

We arrive at an island (let's hope it's Yonder) at 

> We arrive at the island. A single cove seems to be the only good way to set anchor. A 6 armed Cyclops eyes us and our ship as we arrive.

The coastline is filled with ruins. There's a large lighthouse where we see the Cyclops. It's built on top of one of the ruins - but clearly newer than them.

The bay itself holds some crates, but from the bay a rough path leads through the mountain chain surrounding it.

We dock, and as soon as we dock - we hear the alarm bells. (Song: Arriving on the Island of Yonder)
- We bring: [Kyrah](wiki:kyrah), Volon, Bulbug, and the 4 of us.
- We also set the Antikythera for "The Bear", and Thyphoon aims it for the area around [Aresia](wiki:aresia).

A large group comes our way. Currently 150 ft, coming from the lighthouse (or another tower).
- 16 soldiers, 2 rows of 8 with a shieldwall (Phalanx).
- 2 gygans
- One fancy looking guy.

They take up 40 feet in width, 60 feet in depth.
- Row of 8 soldiers
- Row of 8 soldiers
- 2 Gygans
- Captain

We get rage - resistance to bludg, pierce, slashing.
I plan to summon beasts.
- 1 giant octopus (10 feet speed, but can grapple - https://roll20.net/compendium/dnd5e/Giant%20Octopus#content) - though it can only grapple 1 enemy at a time.
- Tiger - decent damage, https://roll20.net/compendium/dnd5e/Tiger#content (1d10)
- https://www.hipstersanddragons.com/conjure-animals-5e-dnd/

And we freeze time at this point to continue another month!

2026-05-02
## Recap vorige sessie
- We went to [the Fates](wiki:the-fates) to pay our debt. Unsuccessfully.
- We met [Hamun Kost](wiki:hamun-kost) on our way to [Island of Yonder](wiki:island-of-yonder)

## This session
Starting at Days 2

We resume at the start of the battle

>We get rage - resistance to bludg, pierce, slashing.
 I plan to summon beasts.

I will summon: 8 giant owls
- 19 hp each
	- 3 of the flock 1 dead
	- 1 of flock 2 dead
	- flock 2-1: 1hp
	- flock 2-2: 
- 1 hour duration
- https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/16889-giant-owl

nat 20 on a flock of owls

We get two waves of enemies coming our way. The Gygans all make a beeline straight for me.
They're very much killed (wave 1) by a fireball and the owls, with some spare extras.

I'm in the bell tower, 150ft away. Together with [Thyphoon](wiki:thyphoon).
- One owl will fly our way - 60 ft per turn
	- Turn 1: 120 ft
- Second owl will come - 150ft + 90, 120 per turn, 2 turns.
- The Gygan we saw here before is now gone
- Thyphoon silenced the bell

I find pages in the tower:

```
My dearest Helena,

Forgive the haste in this letter. I cannot say when another supply ship may carry word from this cursed rock, and I swear I have left too much undsaid for too long.

Two years now I have worn the cerulean cloak and served the order of the island they call yonder. Two years too many. When father set the cape upon my shoulders, he spoke of Sydon's glory, of the Lord of Storms restoring Thylea to her Rightful might. He did not speak of the bones.

They are everywhere here, sister. The bones of giants slaughtered five hundred years gone in the first war, when the dragonlords burned this place to ash. Their kin still walk among us. Two of the creatures serve in our garrison, and I tell you they have not forgotten. They watch the sea each dawn with a hunger I have no words for. You will recall the old sailors' tale of the lost ship - the Ultros, they named her, vanished into the deeps these long centuries - and her captain, the mad dragonlord whose cruelties against the giants the songs no longer sing aloud. To the folk of Mytros it is only a story now. To the gygans here, Helena, it is a wound that has never closed. Marchion has warned us plainly: should that ship somehow ride into our ove again, no command of his nor even of commander Gaius could stay the Gygans' wrath. I have seen what a single one of them does to a man with bare hands. I have no wish to see it again.

But it is not the Gygans that drive me to write. It is the Library.

You must tell no one what Follows. Burn this letter when it is read.

Commander Gaius prepares for war. The oath of peace fails within two moons, perhaps less, and Sydon's fleet gathers already in numbers beyond counting to fall upon Mytros itself. Helena, take mother and leave the city before the next moon turns. Go inland. Go to the oldwood if you must. The order means to put every priest of the Five to the torch, and the common folk who once knelt in their temples shall fare no better.

There is a horned mage who dwells here. He does not serve Sydon at all. He served the Lady of Dreams in secret - the acolytes whisper it when they think no one listens. He keeps a bronze bowl in his chambers and speaks to a Thing in its waters that is not of our world. The prisoners we drag from the shipwrecks are not questioned, sister. They are unmade. I have heard a man scream for three nights and then babble like an infant for three more. And the altar in the courtyard, where the priests claim to burn only beasts as offering to Sydon. I have seen the human bones mixed in among the ash with my own eyes.

So I have decided. I am done with the storm-god and his fleet of butchers. Last night I knelt in the Gygan ruins where no captain would think to look for me, and I prayed, not to Sydon, but to Her. to Thylea. The great mother, whose name still passes the lips of the village folk at harvest and at the breaking of winter, even as Sydon's priests grow louder year by year. I felt warmth move through the cold stones beneath my knees, and something old and patient stirring far below, as though roots had at last begun to open their eyes. I think she heard me, Helena. I think she has been waiting all this long while for me to find my way back to her.

I mean to slip away when the next supply ship arrives and pray the mother hides me from Sydon's eye. If I reach the oldwood, I will send word. If I do not - know that I tried, in the end, to be a better man than the one who left.

...

But sister, wait. There is a ship coming into the cave, I can see her sails from the watchwindow now. The shape of her hull, the cut of her prow - gods preserve me, it cannot be. It is only a story. Only a story the old sailors tell. But by all the five, I swear to you it is the Ultr<BLOODSPATTERS>
```

We found multiple ripped apart soldiers in the lighthouse. Likely ripped apart by the Gygan we saw when we arrived.

The bloodthirsty/raging Gygan that we saw in the lighthouse bursts out of the doors - where [Kyrah](wiki:kyrah) just happens to be, as she for some f\*cking reason went to the lighthouse.

I fire the flares - and they're pending.

[Thyphoon](wiki:thyphoon) jumps down, hanggliding/hangcrashing down on the last remaining eagle to the ground. He jumps off at the last moment when in range of the maddened Gygan - and he throws his lightning javelin at it.

Starting at Day 3, at 01:00

We're preparing an ambush on a bunch of guards guarding the library.

We jump down and attack

The guards are dead, and we rush to the colonnade with the barracks.

Atyche is hit by the song of the harpies and tries to walk towards the statue with the caged harpies on top. Brax grapples her and drags her towards the barracks/commander's quarters, whatever it is. It's the same place where we see a huge statue of Sydon that's clearly moving.

Atyche snaps out of it at the end of her next turn.

Gaius walks in. He walks to the statue of Sydon and starts praying. His golden armour starts sparkling, his sword is sparkling with lightning. He yells *ATTAAAACK!*. We hear rumbling coming from several of the corridors as more enemies barrel our way.

All in all, we now have:
- Gaius, sparkling
- The statue of Sydon, slightly moving
- A gygan and a commander who came into the temple from the side

- Most enemies are blown to bits with a fireball
- I'm brought back up by Thyphoon.
- Gaius is killed by Brax. The statue's eyes dim.

As the fight calms down with the death of Gaius, we now notice the rumbling of starting thunder, and rain pattering outside.

Brax finds a letter in the pocket of Gaius:

> Divine Sydon, lord of all,
> 
> We have received thy orders, and we seek to execute them faithfully. We are overjoyed to hear that thy fleets have been readied for the invasion. Little time remains to the accursed oath, and the simpering masses of Mytros will soon prostrate themselves at thy glorious feet, as is right and proper.
> 
> We have but one concern, and that is the continued presence of the horned mage, Lutheria's pet. He does not participate in our daily sacrifices, and my men do not trust him. Can he not be dismissed?
> 
> Thy eternal servant, Gaius.

Thyphoon fixes the Antikythera, so we can now travel to all islands in the forgotten sea.

Kyrah is not necessarily happy that Gaius is dead, but she's happy that whatever he was doing has stopped.

I enter Gaius' quarters.
- On his desk, there's a pile of love letters to "Argyn", his dragon. From it, we deduce that he recently bought her a present - a Sapphire. She's not yet mature and thus not yet bonded. He was _not_ yet fucking his dragon.
- The rest of the letters were communication between him and his soldiers, and every letter speaks of his fanatical devotion. He gave his entire life to Sydon, and had nothing besides Sydon and his dragon.
- I find my old boots again. When I pick them up, a feeling of warmth and recognition fills me of having refound my old gear again.
- We also find 240 gp and a brilliant blue sapphire worth of 1000 gold pieces

We find the cells. The guard is sleeping. 
- One is absolutely raving mad, it seems like. [Enygma](wiki:enygma).
- Another has a fancy white gear, a top hat with bronze gears, all kinds of gears on his armor. [Mikhael](wiki:mikhael).

The white one with gears:
- His ship crashed and he stranded here, the local populace locked me away. His ship with an "engine" is still in the water somewhere.

We bring both of them with us.
- We also find a room with fresco's depicting the invasion of Mytros.
- On one of the walls: "Glory to Sydon. The oath of peace is ending."
- The last room is the mess hall.

In the meantime, Atyche and Bibi are resting next to the corpse of Gaius. Brax and Kyrah went to the library - finding an absolute wall of rain outside, and the clocktower having stopped.

**We level up!**

We all go to the library, taking [Mikhael](wiki:mikhael) and [Enygma](wiki:enygma) with us. In the meantime, they found the book we were looking for.

### The arrival of the dragonlords
*A scroll, found in the library on the [Island of Yonder](wiki:island-of-yonder)*.

> The Arrival of the Dragonlords
Their siblings gone, Sydon and Lutheria ruled supreme
over the lands of Thylea, worshipped and honored
by the gygans, centaurs, nymphs and other fey. Ages
passed, and the dead Titans were forgotten by the chil-
dren they had created. As far as history remembered,
the Twin Titans were the authors of all.
But the remote continent birthed from their mother
could not remain hidden forever. As the centuries
passed, the so-called civilized races, humans, elves,
dwarves and their like, began to stumble across the
islands at the far reaches of the Forgotten Sea. The first
to arrive were refugees and castaways, survivors of ships
gone astray. Half-drowned, they crawled onto island
shores and carved out a meager existence among the
native fey races.
Sydon ignored these newcomers. They were too weak
and pathetic to acknowledge. Lutheria found something
compelling in their nature. When others came, the
explorers and settlers, she stayed Sydon’s fury and allowed
them to land safely so she could study these strange folk.
As their numbers grew, the civilized races established
small villages along the coasts. Bit by bit, they spread
across the islands of Thylea, until their numbers brought
them into conflict with the original inhabitants.
At first, the civilized races suffered losses when-
ever they encountered the fey folk. They had neither
the strength nor numbers to challenge the gygans or
centaurs in battle. They lacked the power to resist the
magic tricks and temptations of the nymphs, dryads
and satyrs. Everything changed with the arrival of the
Dragonlords, a band of heroes who fought astride great
winged mounts.
Their leader was Xander Huorath, with his mighty
silver dragon, Balmytria. The second in command,
Xander’s chief rival, was Rizon Phobas, who rode
Balmytria’s mate, a great bronze dragon. Joining them
were Adonis Neurdagon, beautiful and vain; the broth-
ers Telamok and Estor Arkelandor, ruthless and savage
warriors; and several others who have since been
forgotten. Each warrior was oathsworn to a dragon, and
together, they were nigh unstoppable in battle.
The arrival of these magnificent creatures stoked
Lutheria’s fascination with the newcomers. The dragons
were unlike anything found in Thylea. At his sister’s
urging, Sydon ignored the pleading of his worshippers
to cleanse Thylea of the invaders. Under the leadership
of the Dragonlords, the civilized races entered an age of
unprecedented expansion.
Villages became towns, and towns grew into great
walled cities. Encounters between the newcomers
and the native races became more frequent, and more
violent. Now the newcomers were winning. The native
races were pushed back, retreating into the unexplored
wilds. Still, out of respect for his sister-wife’s curiosity,
Sydon held his fury in check, just waiting an inevitable
spark that would ignite the fires of all-out war.
He did not have to wait long.

---

fields.summary: Mezz swears his oath to me, Thyphoon's Dream on Versi reveals the paradoxes, and a paradox token skips us to the Island of the Fates.

notes.body:
Started at 2026-10-18 - 20:22
## Recap vorige sessie
- We fought and killed [Gaius](wiki:gaius)
- We freed [Enygma](wiki:enygma)
- We found the scroll "The arrival of the Dragonlords"
## This session
- [Thyphoon](wiki:thyphoon) talks to [Mezz](wiki:mezz) about what he wants to do next. It's a philosophical discussion.

Mezz tells us that the other tunnels on the [Island of the Fates](wiki:island-of-the-fates) lead to other planes of existence. One of them leads to the Underdark and that's how Mezz traveled from the island of the fates to [Island of Yonder](wiki:island-of-yonder).

Mezz's suspicion is that [Chondrus](wiki:chondrus) would've given us accurate information to lead us to the [Nether Sea](wiki:nether-sea), but he would still have passed on all information to [Lutheria](wiki:lutheria-titan).

The oath, which I will take:
- Mezz will be free either when Lutheria is vanquished or I have been dead for a week.
- The oath is considered broken by him if he knowingly or intentionally helps out Lutheria or Sydon, thus betraying us.
- If I am contacted by Lutheria, Sydon or someone affiliated with them, or know of some other form of harm intended for them, I will tell them - I will not actively harm the fellowship through inaction.
- In exchange, we will attempt our best to keep him safe, and we will give him opportunities to build up a better life after his servitude has ended.

[Oath of Mezz to Yendithas](wiki:oath-of-mezz-to-yendithas)

After the oath, he already tells us that [Lutheria](wiki:lutheria-titan) actively keeps track of us due to the time travel. Due to the ripples in the time continuum, she knows where we're active.

- [Thyphoon](wiki:thyphoon) and [Brax](wiki:brax) go to the sacrificial altar of Sydon, and carve through one of his symbols with the Tree of Life.
- We decide to run to the [Ultros](wiki:ultros).
- I use telepathy to communicate with someone aboard the Ultros to let them know we're coming, and to ask them to travel to the docks. I have 24 hours of Telepathy so we can keep telling them when we're close so they can send out a rowboat. With [Volon](wiki:volon).
- We set the [Antikythera](wiki:antikythera) for the Bard, to arrive at the [Island of the Fates](wiki:island-of-the-fates).

We walk through the main entrance and walk towards the docks.
- Before then, we see 20-30 soldiers standing at the docks.
- Brax convinces them to kill each other to get on the Ultros to escape. 10 remain and follow us. [Norak](wiki:norak), the strongest looking of the group, tells us they will follow. The rest falls in line.
- Volon tells me telepathically that [Versi](wiki:versi) is not doing so well.

We go to Versie, Thyphoon and I.
- She's convulsing, blood from her mouth.
- She keeps saying "the thread has been cut before the knot. The thread has been cut before the knot..."
- Apparently this has been happening since we killed Chondrus, becoming worse since Gaius' death.
- Yeah, this is due to us causing a time paradox by killing those two.

Thyphoon casts [Dream](https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2079-dream) on Versi.
- Gaining DM inspiration for the action.
- They see landscape of Thylea. Burning. It looks like floating mirrors, all broken, everywhere.
- Versi is floating in between the mirrors, being "consumed" by the visions.
- They see a man on a dragon, attacking a group of men - and suddenly the man is gone. (day 8, [Session 19](wiki:session-19), confrontation with Gaius)
- They see a colliseum full of people, where there are suddenly two empty spots. (the games, somewhere on day 22-29, [Session 29](wiki:session-29))
- The largest mirror of all shows a group of people walking into a throne room - where two chairs are suddenly empty. (day 11, [Session 22](wiki:session-22))

She sees two realities that can't both be true but must - there MUST be people on those chairs
- We must reconcile the information we would now miss causing us to be in this place.

The DM gives us 6 tokens, standing for 6 paradoxes. They will be used to randomly skip us forward in time. It's not clear how exactly.
- Because we fucked around with time, it will influence when the Oath of Peace ends. That will still happen - but how fast we get there might change.
- We _can_ fix this by fixing the three paradoxes. For each one we fix for either Gaius or Chondrus, one token is gone.

We stepped on board of the Ultros on relative day 3, absolute day 50, around 03:00.

While we're doing all kinds of things on board, at 3 in the morning... It suddenly is clear day and we've arrived at the island of the fates. It's now day 5 at 12:00. *One token is gone.*
- According to Volon, we were in half zombie state.
- Apparently, the ship has taken damage from the thunder?
- The eggs are still safe.
- Versi knows what happened to us.

notes.title: Summoning the New Gods
notes.body:
> "Some say that it was the Dragonlords who summoned [the Five](wiki:the-five) Gods. Others say that it was the silver dragon, [Balmytria](wiki:balmytria). So much time has passed now; the truth may never be known. 
> —Aesop, Keeper of the Dragon Shrine

At the beginning of the First War the civilized peoples won many victories. Led by the Dragonlords, they rode roughshod over the armies of the Titans. The children of [Thylea](wiki:thylea-titan) could not stand against the great dragons and were routed time and time again.

The armies of gygans and centaurs prayed to [Sydon](wiki:sydon-titan) and [Lutheria](wiki:lutheria-titan) for aid, crying out to the Twins to save them from extinction. They begged the Titans to destroy the dragons, so that they could meet the civilized races in equal strength on the battlefield.

Sydon and Lutheria heard their laments and joined the struggle. The tide of war turned in favor of the native races: even a dragon cannot stand against a Titan. Whenever the dragons took to the skies, Sydon lashed them with raging winds and blasts of lightning, forcing them to the ground, where they became vulnerable to the wrath of Lutheria, who assailed them with her wicked scythe and death magic.

Many dragons were lost, and others fled. But the silver dragon, Balmytria, knew that Lutheria and Sydon would eventually find them all. In her final stand against the tyranny of the Titans, the silver dragon threw herself heedlessly against them, tearing and clawing, even after suffering numerous mortal injuries. When at last her energy was exhausted, she collapsed to the ground dead, and the Twins spat on her corpse.

Balmytria’s death ripped a hole in the very fabric of reality that rippled throughout the multiverse. Inspired by her sacrifice, five celestial beings answered her prayer and came to Thylea to protect her people. These beings are known as the Five Gods, who we still worship today: [Mytros](wiki:mytros-god), [Volkan](wiki:volkan), [Pythor](wiki:pythor), [Vallus](wiki:vallus) and [Kyrah](wiki:kyrah).

The Five pledged themselves to protect the civilized races, restoring the balance of power. In the years that followed, an uneasy truce was brokered, creating a peace that has lasted for 500 years.

In any case, this is how the story is usually told...

notes.title: Sydon (Titan)

- A colossal, bearded man with three eyes, carrying a terrifying black glaive. Summons storms to punish those who displease him.
- Jealous and vengeful: allows worship of no god but himself and Lutheria. Daily sacrifices are offered to him in every village. Thunder means someone has provoked his anger.

notes.title: The Birth of the Titans
notes.body:
In the beginning, the islands of [Thylea](wiki:thylea) were populated
only by harmless plants and gentle animals—the flora
and fauna a reflection of the nurturing spirit of the
Mother Goddess that sacrificed herself to create them.
A virgin paradise, the Forgotten Land was kept safe from
the perils and evils of the outside world by the giant
[Kentimane](wiki:kentimane-titan) of the Hundred Hands—Thylea’s lover and
protector. And together, the two were content.
But one day, the tree at the center of the islands—the
transformed heart of the Mother Goddess herself—
blossomed with seven strange fruits. Each the size of a
boulder, they shimmered and pulsed with vibrant, shift-
ing colors, almost as if alive. Seeing the tempting bounty
sprouting from the branches, Kentimane reached from
the ocean and plucked the fruit. His fifty heads gorged
themselves on the succulent flesh, tearing and chewing
until all that remained were seven spike-covered pits,
which he tossed into the ocean.

Instead of sinking, the pits floated on the waves,
bobbing up and down. Offended by their taunting
presence, Kentimane seized each pit in a clenched fist,
squeezing so hard the spikes bit into his flesh and drew
blood. Howling in rage, Kentimane slammed the pits
down beneath the water, burying them deep beneath the
muddy bottom of the ocean floor.

But the next morning the pits floated back up to
the surface. Before Kentimane could seize them again,
the pits burst open and the children of Thylea and
Kentimane sprang forth into existence.

The hundred-handed god stared in wonder at his
offspring: eight Titans born from the fruit of Thylea’s
tree, fertilized by the blood of Kentimane himself. Each
of the first six pits had incubated a single child blessed
with a different attribute drawn from one of their par-
ents: Strength; Beauty; Wisdom; Craft; Prophecy and
Swiftness. As these six Titans grew from children into
adults, they became demi-gods, each representing the
aspect of their parents they most embodied.

However, from the seventh pit two Titans were born:
[Sydon](wiki:sydon-titan) and [Lutheria](wiki:lutheria-titan), twin brother and sister. Sydon
embodied his father’s raging fury, and as he grew he
became the God of Time and the Lord of Storms. His
sister, Lutheria, inherited her mother’s stillness and
calm... but without Thylea’s compassion or gentleness,
she would eventually become the Goddess of Death and
the Lady of Dreams.

But all this was far in the future, and Kentimane did
not foresee what his offspring would one day become.
He could not imagine the strife and suffering the Twins
would bring to the peaceful islands. If he had known,
he might have drowned them on the spot. But instead,
he scooped up his children from the waves—including
Sydon and Lutheria—and placed them gently at the base
of the great Heart-Tree rising up from the center of the
island, where Thylea could watch over them.

Having deposited the children in the warm bosom
of their mother, Kentimane returned to the sea and
resumed his eternal vigil, bound by his sacred vow to
keep Thylea—and now also their children—safe from
the outside world.

notes.title: The Creation of the Fey Races
notes.body:
For a time the eight children of [Thylea](wiki:thylea-titan) and [Kentimane](wiki:kentimane-titan)
lived quiet and contented lives, sheltered on the islands
spawned from the body of their mother. But, in time,
contentment became loneliness. They were gods, but
they had no purpose.

[Talieus - The Bald, Blind Titan](wiki:talieus-titan), the God of Crafting, first born of the siblings,
gathered his younger brothers and sisters together
and proposed they create races of mortal creatures to
worship and revere them. Of all the Titans, only [Sydon](wiki:sydon-titan)
and [Lutheria](wiki:lutheria-titan), his youngest siblings, refused: they were
united by the powerful bond, and did not feel the empty
loneliness of their kin.

The other Titans created centaurs, satyrs and nymphs,
who quickly spread to populate the islands. Next, they
created the cyclopes and gygans, great giants capable
of moving earth and stone to build massive temples in
honor of Talieus and the others who had given them life.
Sydon and Lutheria regarded these new mortal races
with contempt. They became bitter and resentful, and
isolated themselves on the last uninhabited island of
Thylea, where their hatred festered.

One day, Lutheria approached [Talieus - The Bald, Blind Titan](wiki:talieus-titan), claiming she
and her twin had grown weary of their solitude. Offering
praise and flattery, she urged him to create a new race,
one greater than all the others, to dwell on her island.
Weakened by his sister’s adulation, [Talieus - The Bald, Blind Titan](wiki:talieus-titan) did as he
was bade and the myrmekes were born. An industrious,
insect-like race with a shared hive-mind intelligence, the
myrmekes quickly spread out from their isolated home,
overwhelming and conquering the native species on
nearby islands. The other Titans condemned Talieus for 
creating such aggressive and dangerous creatures. Talieus, burning with
parental pride, refused act against his newest children. It
fell to Sydon, the God of Storms, to halt the [Myrmekes](wiki:myrmekes)’
advance. As they piled into their ships, he unleashed the
fury of the sea, dashing their vessels to smithereens with
howling winds, drowning them beneath the waves. Even
Sydon could not halt their advance forever. The other
Titans, fearful the [Myrmekes](wiki:myrmekes) would continue to spread,
begged their father for help. Moved by the fears of his
children, Kentimane used his hundred hands to gather all
the myrmekes onto a single island. Calling on the strength
of Thylea herself, he bound them there with powerful
magic so they could never leave.

As punishment for his foolishness and pride,
Kentimane stripped Talieus of his power and gave it to
Sydon. Using his older brother’s former power against
him, Sydon bound Talieus and presented him to his
sister and now wife as a gift.

Lutheria took no pity on her helpless elder brother.
She blinded the mighty Titan and sewed his lips shut, so
he could never tell the others the truth of his downfall.
Then she bound his power to her crystal scythe and
forced him to wander eternally in the Nether Sea, 
dragging her throne-ship across the waves behind him by a
great chain strapped around his neck.

Seeing Talieus’ fate, the other Titans were horrified.
Together they began plotting revenge against the twins,
but Lutheria and Sydon were ready for them.

notes.title: The fates
notes.body:
3 ladies that determine the fate of everyone in [Thylea](wiki:thylea).

The bosslady snips the thread of fate of anyone who dies.

Not even the titans trust them.

They were the ones who sealed the Oath of Peace.

What they can do for us:

-   Completely, in detail, explain 3 islands in the Cerulean Sea.
-   Resurrect any number of corpses.
-   Give us experience.
-   They can create magical items with their looms - but they won’t tell us which ones.
-   Answer specific questions about the past, present or future.

For each of these, the rule is: the easier the feat is, the cheaper it will be.

notes.title: The Titans
notes.body:
The Titans are divine powers native to [Thylea](wiki:thylea). They have existed since the dawn of time. The two Titans still free, [Sydon](wiki:sydon-titan) and [Lutheria](wiki:lutheria-titan), are our enemies and those of [The Five](wiki:the-five).

## The Ancient Titans

**[Thylea](wiki:thylea-titan)**, the Great Mother, is the namesake of the Lost Land (the mainland, [Thylea](wiki:thylea)). She takes the form of a gargantuan tree on an island at the heart of the Cerulean Gulf, and her followers believe that her roots reach deep into the earth, binding the world together in an eternal embrace. She is believed to be a generous, life-giving goddess. The Druids of the Oldwood believe that her will is communicated through the changing of the seasons, rather than through words: long winters signal her displeasure, long summers her approval.

**[Kentimane](wiki:kentimane-titan)** was the most powerful of the Titans. He is believed to be both the husband and eternal guardian of the Great Mother. Many references to him are found in the poetry of the gygans and the centaurs, but few credible sources have survived the ravages of time. Usually depicted with one hundred heads and one hundred hands.

**[Sydon](wiki:sydon-titan)** is the Lord of the Oceans and all that flows from them. He takes the form of a colossal, bearded man with three eyes, and carries a terrifying black glaive. He surveys both land and water tirelessly, summoning storms to punish those who displease him. A jealous and vengeful god who makes no allowances for the worship of any god but himself or his sister-wife, Lutheria.
- Every temple in Thylea fears his wrath. Daily sacrifices are offered to him in every village, even as the settlers continue their silent prayers to the Five. Whenever thunder rolls through the skies of Thylea, someone has provoked his anger.

**[Lutheria](wiki:lutheria-titan)** takes the form of a beautiful, black-eyed woman who sleepwalks through the underworld, greeting the spirits of the dead. She carries a crystal scythe, which she uses to harvest the souls of those who displeased her in life. She commands her followers to live without remorse, to drink, dance and feast to their heart's desire, because any day could be their last. She is a mother to the fey races of Thylea, whom she strongly favors.
- Worship of Lutheria is rare among settlers, but she is nevertheless honored with many feasts and festivals because Sydon demands it. Whenever any drink is poured, a libation must be made to her, or a swift punishment is sure to follow.

## The children of Thylea and Kentimane

Eight Titans, born from seven fruits of [Thylea](wiki:thylea-titan)'s heart-tree ([The Birth of the Titans](wiki:the-birth-of-the-titans)):

| Titan | Aspect | Fate |
|---|---|---|
| [Talieus](wiki:talieus-titan) | Craft (first born) | Enslaved by Sydon, power bound to Lutheria's scythe, drags her throne-ship through the [Nether Sea](wiki:nether-sea) |
| [Hergeron](wiki:hergeron-titan) | Strength and Valor | Imprisoned beneath a great tower by Sydon |
| [Chalcia](wiki:chalcia-titan) | Swiftness | Entombed beneath the volcano of [Fire Island](wiki:fire-island). We gave her more room; she can escape once Sydon is dead ([Session 49](wiki:session-49)) |
| *(unnamed)* | Beauty, Wisdom, Prophecy | Three Titans turned to stone by Lutheria's basilisk-blood trap |
| [Sydon](wiki:sydon-titan) | Raging fury: God of Time, Lord of Storms | One of the two remaining Titans, with Lutheria |
| [Lutheria](wiki:lutheria-titan) | Stillness without compassion: Goddess of Death, Lady of Dreams | Twin and wife of Sydon |

notes.title: The War of the Titans
notes.body:
For a time the children of [Thylea](wiki:thylea-titan) and [Kentimane](wiki:kentimane-titan) dwelt
together in peace. But after [Lutheria](wiki:lutheria-titan) and Sydon enslaved
their eldest brother for creating the [Myrmekes](wiki:myrmekes), the
remaining siblings decided upon revenge.

[Hergeron](wiki:hergeron-titan), the second eldest brother and the god of
Strength and Valor, challenged [Sydon](wiki:sydon-titan) to a duel, brashly
confident in his own abilities. But Sydon had absorbed
much of the enslaved [Talieus - The Bald, Blind Titan](wiki:talieus-titan)’ power, and he easily
bested his challenger. Sydon imprisoned the defeated
Hergeron beneath a great tower, chaining him to so that
the full weight of the building was forever pressing down
on Hergeron’s enormous neck and shoulders.

The remaining four siblings, realizing Sydon had
grown too powerful to challenge directly, decided to
strike at Lutheria. In secret, they traveled to her island
but the Goddess of Death had set a trap for her kin.
Through the ritual sacrifice of a thousand basilisks, she
had created a great pool of poisonous blood at the heart
of her domain. When the invaders set foot upon the
island they triggered wards of power that released the
magic of the foul pool in a lethal burst, instantly turning
three of them to stone. Only [Chalcia](wiki:chalcia-titan), the Goddess of
Swiftness, was nimble enough to escape.
Knowing the Twins would come after her, Chalcia
took shelter beneath a massive volcano. There she could use 
her speed and quickness to survive in the labyrinth
of tunnels and lava tubes. When Sydon learned of the
failed attack against his sister-wife, his fury knew no
bounds. In a blind rage, he summoned a great storm to
lash all the islands of Thylea, seeking to flood the cham-
bers where Chalcia was hiding.
The storms threatened to wash away Thylea itself,
something that Kentimane would not allow. Kentimane
had stayed neutral in the battles of his children but,
once the safety of all of Thylea became threatened, he
was forced to intervene. Kentimane blunted the storms,
and he forbade Sydon and Lutheria from destroying the
volcano that sheltered their fugitive sister. Sydon was
loathe to let Chalcia escape retribution, but even he was
not strong enough to defy his mighty father. Lutheria,
cunning as ever, knew of another way to get revenge.
Uniting their power, and the power stolen from their
fallen siblings, the Twins reached deep into the foun-
dation of Thylea. They shifted rock and stone, careful
not to disturb the islands above as they sealed off the
tunnels and chambers beneath the volcano one by one.
Chalcia ran from their relentless work, driven ever
deeper beneath the earth. In the end, the elusive Goddess
of Swiftness found herself trapped in a tiny chamber
at the very heart of the volcano itself. With every exit
sealed, the walls slowly closed in tighter and tighter as
burning lava oozed through cracks and crevices in floor
and ceiling. Instead of crushing her, the Twins stopped at
the last instant, entombing their sister for all eternity in a
crypt of searing heat and noxious fumes.

notes.title: Thylea (Titan)
notes.body:
One of [The Titans](wiki:the-titans): the Great Mother. Not to be confused with the mainland, [Thylea](wiki:thylea), which is named after her.

- Takes the form of a gargantuan tree on an island at the heart of the Cerulean Gulf. Her followers believe that her roots reach deep into the earth, binding the world together in an eternal embrace.
- A generous, life-giving goddess. The Druids of the Oldwood believe her will is communicated through the changing of the seasons: long winters signal her displeasure, long summers her approval.
- Wife of [Kentimane](wiki:kentimane-titan), who guards her. Mother of the other Titans, born from the fruits of her heart-tree ([The Birth of the Titans](wiki:the-birth-of-the-titans)).
- At a tree, [Thyphoon](wiki:thyphoon) asks her how we can befriend [the Amazons](wiki:the-amazons) ([Session 53](wiki:session-53)). She appears to us as Mother Thylea and shows us a vision of the birth of the Titans ([Session 54](wiki:session-54)).

notes.title: Titan's Folley
notes.body:
Sterrenbeeld “The End”

Hier kunnen de Fates ook weinig van vertellen.

[Kentimane](wiki:kentimane-titan) heeft hier een glass dome omheen gezet. Zelfs de fates kunnen niet zien wat er hieronder is.

Wat er over gezegd kan worden:

- Er leeft een onbekend ras dat verder op [Thylea](wiki:thylea) niet te vinden is, genaamd “[Myrmekes](wiki:myrmekes)”. Niemand heeft ze ooit gezien. De leider van de groep heet KCHKWHHAA (onbekende taal).
- De dome staat er al zo’n 50.000 jaar.
- 3 perfectly molded green hills.
- Encompassed by a giant glass dome.
- Can be bypassed by teleportation magic.
- _Must be avoided at all cost._
- Rumored to be the home of Thylea's greatest treasure.    
- Sealed away by Kentimane as a result of the first war of the gods (so not the war of the dragonlords)
- Known by all fishermen, for the legend says that it is the home of Thylea’s greatest treasure.

notes.title: Ultros
notes.body:
The ancient ship of the first war, found by us in a hidden cave at the Dead Falls and now our ship. [Yendithas](wiki:yendithas) is its captain. Crew: [Crew of the Ultros](wiki:crew-of-the-ultros). We navigate it to islands with the [Antikythera](wiki:antikythera).

## History
- First seen in a dream after drinking from the [Horn of Balmytria](wiki:horn-of-balmytria): a galley on which we are the captain and the 15 other sailors are dead and skeletal. [Kyrah](wiki:kyrah) told us it was the ghost ship Ultros ([Session 11](wiki:session-11), [Day 4](wiki:day-4)).
- Captained by [Estor Arklander](wiki:estor-arklander) in the first war. After the war he destroyed all gygans ([Session 40](wiki:session-40)).
- [Sydon](wiki:sydon-titan) unleashed his fury to drag it down, but the magic of the Ultros was too strong ([Session 27](wiki:session-27), [Session 40](wiki:session-40)).
- [Lutheria](wiki:lutheria-titan) offered Estor and his crew eternal life if he stopped his rampage. He slit the throats of his officers as a blood sacrifice and the crew rose again. They could still be hurt and feel pain. They never broke the curse, and after centuries only their spirits remained to crew the ship ([Session 40](wiki:session-40)).
- Per [Session 43](wiki:session-43): the titans' revenge blow slaughtered most of the dragonlords, including Estor, captain of the Ultros. This is largely unaccounted.
- Several years after the war it disappeared ([Session 27](wiki:session-27)).

## Finding and taking command ([Day 32](wiki:day-32))
- The last known location was on a map from King [Acustus](wiki:acustus): the Dead Falls, the rocky wastelands of the east ([Session 38](wiki:session-38), [Session 40](wiki:session-40)).
- It lay in a secret inlet behind a silent waterfall, reached through a small underwater tunnel ([Session 40](wiki:session-40)).
- About 70 ghost crew, ethereal oarmen, an ethereal drummer, and Estor's journal in the captain's room. A locked box held 16 onyx gemstones. Removing them spawned a specter.
- In a dream Estor chose a successor. We had to swear the oath (see [Oaths](wiki:oaths)): "I swear upon my life's blood that I shall captain the Ultros with honour. Even were she to sail into the maw of the [Nether Sea](wiki:nether-sea), my fate shall be bound to hers." We then killed the traitors Davos (quartermaster), Metron (navigator) and Skathon (first mate) ([Session 41](wiki:session-41)).
- Estor offered Yendithas the title of captain together with his powers. Yendithas refused the powers, but we can control the ship.
- It can travel underwater ([Session 41](wiki:session-41)).
- King [Acustus](wiki:acustus) called it a "relic of bygone days" ([Session 42](wiki:session-42), [Day 33](wiki:day-33)).

## Outfitting
- 4 ballistae and 2 rowboats ([Session 42](wiki:session-42)). Later crew in [Crew of the Ultros](wiki:crew-of-the-ultros).

## Voyages
- Sailed into the storm with the help of [Kentimane](wiki:kentimane-titan), dived under the sea and ended up before [Khronos](wiki:khronos), who sent us and the ship back in time ([Session 52](wiki:session-52), [Day 41](wiki:day-41)).
- [Session 66](wiki:session-66): traveling to the island of the Chimera.
- [Session 72](wiki:session-72): seen from the library on [Island of Yonder](wiki:island-of-yonder).
- [Day 50](wiki:day-50): boarded around 03:00 with ten soldiers led by [Norak](wiki:norak). On [Day 52](wiki:day-52) it arrived at the [Island of the Fates](wiki:island-of-the-fates), damaged by thunder. The eggs were safe.

notes.title: Vallus
notes.body:
One of [The Five](wiki:the-five) Gods: the Goddess of Wisdom (and beauty). The oldest daughter of [Mytros](wiki:mytros-god), and in many ways the heir to her mother's legacy: queen and patron goddess of the city of [Mytros](wiki:mytros). Wife of King [Acustus](wiki:acustus).

- Believed to know as much about [Thylea](wiki:thylea)'s history as [Sydon](wiki:sydon-titan) and [Lutheria](wiki:lutheria-titan). She used to travel far and wide, surveying ancient ruins and collecting lore about the origins of the land and the fey races.
- Prayers are offered to her when guidance is needed and information is scarce.

- Proposed that [The Five](wiki:the-five) sacrifice part of their divinity to clear Sydon's storm. Told us to bring the [Ultros](wiki:ultros) to her own harbor instead of to Acustus, and gave us the map to it ([Session 22](wiki:session-22), [Session 23](wiki:session-23), [Day 11](wiki:day-11)).

The [Amazons](wiki:the-amazons) in her guard (captain: [Makhaila](wiki:makhaila)) relate closely to her. The horn must be returned to her, and given willingly to no one else.

notes.title: Versi
notes.body:
The lover of [Yendithas](wiki:yendithas)
Has had visions of [Brax](wiki:brax) before we started out.
The daughter of [Sydon](wiki:sydon-titan).
The sister of [Demetria](wiki:demetria)

More info at [How I lost my dragon](wiki:how-i-lost-my-dragon):
*Some things I remember in between: [Versi](wiki:versi) took care of me for 500 years. She has lived for millennia, and she enjoys life, even though she's turned against her father [Sydon](wiki:sydon-titan). She's lived a lonely life... But during the battle of the dragonlords against the titans, she allied with the dragonlords, and served as a sort of "medic" during the battles. When she saw me lying on the field, she was instantly in love, and she did everything she could to save me. She had to put me in statis in her temple, to heal over the last 500 years. But when the prophesy came to her, she saw I had to step up.*

[Day 50](wiki:day-50): convulsing, blood from her mouth, repeating "the thread has been cut before the knot". It started when we killed [Chondrus](wiki:chondrus) and got worse after [Gaius](wiki:gaius) died: a time paradox ([Paradox tokens](wiki:paradox-tokens)). She knew what had happened to us when we reached the [Island of the Fates](wiki:island-of-the-fates) ([Day 52](wiki:day-52)).

- We freed her in the temple of the Oracle. She gave us the three great tasks ([quests](wiki:quests)) and answered one question each about our fate ([Session 4](wiki:session-4), [Session 5](wiki:session-5), [Day 2](wiki:day-2)).

notes.title: Volkan
notes.body:
One of [The Five](wiki:the-five) Gods: the God of Forges. Works the [Mythral Forge](wiki:mythral-forge) together with [Fajra](wiki:fajra).

- Not much is known about him, except that he is the husband of [Mytros](wiki:mytros-god). Father of [Pythor](wiki:pythor).
- Concerns himself with artifice and crafting. Mainly worshipped by dwarves, smiths and wizards.
- Depicted as an elderly, wise-looking man (sometimes as a dwarf).
- Rumored to travel through the Heartlands on the winter solstice, handing out toys and sweets to children.

- In [Estoria](wiki:estoria) we go to him for more info about the theft from the [Dragon Shrine](wiki:dragon-shrine) ([Session 6](wiki:session-6), [Day 3](wiki:day-3)).
- With the hammer of [Pythor](wiki:pythor) he can craft at the [Mythral Forge](wiki:mythral-forge). We order an amulet of health, the Zaphyre Lute and the Euros Lyre ([Session 20](wiki:session-20), [Day 9](wiki:day-9)), later changed to the Boreal Harp and the Euros Lyre. He travels with us to the crossroads ([Session 23](wiki:session-23), [Day 12](wiki:day-12)).
- Back in the [Mythral Mines](wiki:mythral-mines) we find him quarreling with Fajra. They hand us the items we ordered from him: an amulet of health for [Atyche](wiki:atyche), the Euros Lyre and the Boreal Harp ([Session 39](wiki:session-39), [Session 40](wiki:session-40), [Day 31](wiki:day-31)).

notes.title: Volon
notes.body:
Crew of the [Ultros](wiki:ultros) ([Crew of the Ultros](wiki:crew-of-the-ultros)).

- Part of the full crew we assembled when outfitting the Ultros v2.0 in [Mytros](wiki:mytros), with the four of us, [Bullbug](wiki:bullbug-sisi), [Kyrah](wiki:kyrah), [Pythor](wiki:pythor), [Versi](wiki:versi), [Loreas](wiki:loreas), 2 Amazons and 65 sailors ([Session 42](wiki:session-42), [Day 33](wiki:day-33)).
- Sworn brother of [Yendithas](wiki:yendithas), together with Bullbug ([Oaths](wiki:oaths)).
- Came ashore with us and Bullbug on [Fire Island](wiki:fire-island) ([Session 46](wiki:session-46), [Day 38](wiki:day-38)).
- Part of the landing party at [Island of Yonder](wiki:island-of-yonder) with Kyrah, Bullbug and the four of us ([Session 69](wiki:session-69)).
- [Day 50](wiki:day-50): Yendithas reached him by telepathy and he reported that [Versi](wiki:versi) was doing badly. On [Day 52](wiki:day-52) he told us we had been in a half-zombie state ([Session 76](wiki:session-76)).

The older sessions only list him by name; nothing is recorded yet about who he is or what he looks like.

notes.title: Xander Huorath
notes.body:
First and the greatest of the dragonlords.
- [Versi](wiki:versi) told [Yendithas](wiki:yendithas) to talk to him at the [Necropolis at Telamok](wiki:necropolis-at-telamok) ([Session 5](wiki:session-5)).
- Always had a large collection of weapons ([Session 20](wiki:session-20)).
- Authoritarian. [Rison Phobas](wiki:rison-phobas) was his second in command and lifelong rival ([Session 14](wiki:session-14)).

notes.title: Yendithas
notes.body:
Yendithas Gyrahaeras’ former dragon was a great bronze dragon named Naegalor.

Used to be a great dragonlord, still used to being 'strong' (skilltree working towards regaining his old strength)

Blunt but charismatic.

Slept with his back to a wall, stuff held close.

Respect. Everyone deserves it.

No one else should go through what I did.

I'd rather kill someone in their sleep than fight fair.

![](media/pasted-image-20261103150059.jpg)![](media/pasted-image-20261103150116.jpg)
![](media/pasted-image-20261103150129.jpg)

- From the Sword Coast of the "main world"; the rest of the party is from [Thylea](wiki:thylea) ([Session 21](wiki:session-21)).
- Shortbow of Cupidity: [Demetria](wiki:demetria)'s bow, which I got after her death at the [Mossy Temple](wiki:mossy-temple) ([Session 9](wiki:session-9), [Session 10](wiki:session-10)). Sacrificed to [Khronos](wiki:khronos) for 1 day of time travel ([Session 52](wiki:session-52)).

## Epithets

*Homeric style: one main epithet (medium), plus two alternates of other lengths to fit the line.*

- **Short:** Song-weaver
- **Medium:** The long-sleeper (500 years with [Versi](wiki:versi))
- **Long:** Bard who sings storms to silence (calming the waves, [Session 43](wiki:session-43))
